identity.title: ALMA Observations of the Young Substellar Binary System 2M1207

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA observations of the 2M1207 system, a young binary made of a brown dwarf with a planetary-mass companion at a projected separation of about 40 au.

evidence.quote: 2M1207A and b have an angular separation of 0.77$''$, which corresponds to a projected separation of 40.6 au at a distance of 52.8 pc (cite: Ducourant:2008).

distance_source.value: Ducourant et al. 2008; weighted mean of parallaxes (Gizis 2007, Biller 2007, Ducourant 2008)

evidence.quote: 2M1207A and b have an angular separation of 0.77$''$, which corresponds to a projected separation of 40.6 au at a distance of 52.8 pc (cite: Ducourant:2008).

question.value: Do the brown dwarf 2M1207A and its planetary-mass companion 2M1207b host dust and gas disks, and what are their sizes and masses?

evidence.quote: We detect emission from dust continuum at 0.89 mm and from the $J = 3 - 2$ rotational transition of CO from a very compact disk around the young brown dwarf.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.01016.S.
We observed the 2M1207 system using ALMA Early Science in Cycle 2 at Band 7 (frequency of about 338 GHz).

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows, 1.875 GHz each, centered 330.98, 332.93, 342.98, 344.98 GHz; 0.488 MHz channels (0.42 km/s), Hanning smoothed

evidence.quote: Their central frequency is 330.98, 332.93, 342.98 and 344.98 GHz, respectively.
The channel width in these two spectral windows is 0.488 MHz (0.42 km s$^{-1}$ for CO $J = 3 - 2$).
chosen in order to probe possible molecular emission from $^{12}$CO($J = 3 - 2$) and $^{13}$CO($J = 3 - 2$), respectively.
Baseline lengths ranged between 19.6 and 650.3 m.
The angular resolution is $0.42'' \times 0.35''$ which corresponds to a spatial resolution of about 22 au $\times$ 18 au at the distance of 2M1207.
the uncertainty accounts for a rms noise of 26 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$
The total time on-source was approximately 2 hours.
Observations were performed on June 29, July 17 and 18 2014, when 30 antennas were available.

findings_qualitative.value: No dust or CO emission at 2M1207b; 2M1207A dust emission unresolved

evidence.quote: Neither dust emission nor CO J=3-2 line emission were detected at the location of the planetary-mass companion 2M1207b.

claims.hypothesis: Does 2M1207b host a massive circum-planetary dust disk?
claims.experiment: 0.89 mm continuum non-detection converted to dust mass
claims.finding: Tightest dust limit for a young planetary-mass companion; little mm pebble material

evidence.quote: which is the tightest upper limit obtained so far for the mass of dust particles surrounding a young planetary-mass companion

claims.hypothesis: Is the 2M1207A disk compact due to tidal truncation by 2M1207b?
claims.experiment: CO uv-plane fit and Monte Carlo truncation model
claims.result: r_c = 9.4 ± 1.5 au; truncation radius ≳10 au for e ≲ 0.4
claims.finding: Tidal truncation can naturally explain small radius, though independent formation is not ruled out

evidence.quote: The observational data obtained so far cannot rule out any of these two competing mechanisms for the formation of the 2M1207 system.

limitations_admitted.value: CO disk only marginally resolved, giving M sin^2 i degeneracy
